title: What would you need before trusting an AI trading agent with real money?
author: Open_Swimming5859
selftext:
We're building an agentic trading project for the Colosseum hackathon, and feedback from earlier posts has made us rethink quite a few parts of the architecture.

One thing I'm still trying to figure out is where people draw the line between "interesting demo" and "I'd actually let this trade my money."

Our current model is that the agent doesn't get unrestricted wallet access. It gets a limited trading permission with things like a spend cap, and those limits are enforced outside the model.

But even if the agent can't exceed its budget, it can still make terrible trades *inside* that budget.

So for people who have actually run AI/automated trading systems, what would you consider mandatory before letting one trade live?

Things we're currently looking at:

* per-trade limits
* total exposure/spend limits
* slippage protection
* trade-frequency limits
* token/market restrictions
* kill switch
* paper-trading period
* handling duplicate/retried transactions

What am I missing?

Especially interested in cases where the system technically followed all its permissions but still did something stupid economically.

Trying to break as much as possible before the Colosseum submission.

comments.author: Both_Yoghurt1437
comments.body: My trading strategy was built with AI, but I use a trading bot (python script) for my automated trades. There is no AI in the loop.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: You're missing a drawdown circuit breaker. Per-trade caps don't stop an agent from bleeding 20 small losses in a row, so halt the whole thing on cumulative loss, not just per-trade size.
